_doc: Rarity tiers, lowest first; the index (0-4) is LOOT_RARITY. weight = relative drop weight. affixes = [min, max] upside affixes. Chances are per-mille ints: downside_chance (a trade-off affix, which grants one extra upside and raises the budget by downside_budget_pct), unidentified_chance, upgrade_one / upgrade_two (bump the rolled tier after the floor is applied), named_chance (top tier only: award a named.json item instead). budget = item value ceiling in gp by loot level, piecewise-linear; the runtime enforces it with the engine's own GetGoldPieceValue on a forge blank. Anchored to obtainable gear (2026-11-05): p50 24k, p75 130k, p90 1.18M, p95 3.24M of the module's 2,900 accessible items. color = a color.nss constant. roll_bias = each upside's ladder step is the best of (1 + roll_bias) rolls inside its level window. window_shift = ladder steps added to both ends of every UPSIDE window by loot level (piecewise-linear, like budget), clamped to the affix's max_step (lo-power-curve, admin 2026-11-18: rarity now raises each enchantment's strength, not only the count). Budgets re-anchored 2026-11-18 so the shifted windows survive the step-down: a Legendary L60 weapon can carry +16 enhancement with 3-4 other enchantments; the top stays under the most valuable obtainable item (20.8M). sockets = [min, max] gem sockets a rolled item of the tier gets (Phase 5; loot/gems.json, loot/sockets.json max_sockets bounds it). augment_steps = [min, max] ladder rungs an augment (lo-augment-originals) raises one existing property of an original item by, capped at the affix's max_step.
